status: Measured 2026-09-11 on one AWS m7a.4xlarge. Fluree v4.2.1 has the lowest read and durable-write geometric means at all three Pokec scales. All 35 queries complete without execution errors on all four engines. Two read queries have result-count differences at small/medium scale; see REPORT.md section 5, including a comparison excluding both queries.

dataset.name: Pokec (benchgraph / mgbench)
dataset.description: Slovak Pokec social network, Memgraph's published benchgraph distribution. Single :User node label, single Friend relationship type, no edge properties.
dataset.source: deps.memgraph.io (verbatim Memgraph distribution); queries = Neo4j-portable branch of memgraph/tests/mgbench/workloads/pokec.py

methodology.transport: Each engine measured over its real-world client transport, and each client holds ONE persistent connection for the whole run: Fluree over its HTTP/JSON API through a keep-alive http.client connection (bench_runner.py; the previous urllib client opened a new TCP connection per request, ~0.25 ms on this box), Memgraph and Neo4j over Bolt (official neo4j driver 6.3.0), FalkorDB over native RESP (GRAPH.QUERY via falkordb client 1.7.1).
methodology.durability: Per-commit durability configured for all four engines; flush behavior checked with strace over 40 writes (8 queries x 5 runs) on small. Fluree FLUREE_STORAGE_FSYNC=wal; Neo4j default; Memgraph --storage-wal-file-flush-every-n-tx=1; FalkorDB Redis AOF appendfsync always. Counts are in engines/durability/. Syscall counts are not a crash-recovery test.
methodology.clean_protocol: Fresh load -> discarded reads-only pass -> recorded reads-only pass (canonical reads) -> separate full pass (canonical writes). Read measurements precede all write mutations; writes accumulate mutations within their own pass.
methodology.shared_params_all_scales: All three scales measured for all four engines on one box with shared params_<scale>.json (fresh load each). Result-set sizes cross-checked per query across the four engines (see caveats for the known differences).
methodology.containers: Neo4j, Memgraph and FalkorDB run from their official Docker images with --network host (no docker-proxy hop) and named volumes on the same gp3 volume Fluree writes to. Fluree runs natively.
methodology.notes: Single-client isolated latency on current hardware; NOT comparable to Memgraph's published multi-worker throughput/mixed/realistic modes. Absolute times are this-box-only. The July 2026 v4.1.2 report ran on an r8a.4xlarge (Zen 5); its numbers are not directly comparable to this box.

fluree.label: Fluree
fluree.config: Source build (cargo build --release -p fluree-db-cli). Served over the HTTP/JSON API (fluree server run, default log level). FLUREE_STORAGE_FSYNC=wal (per-commit WAL fdatasync), background indexing at the shipped default threshold, FLUREE_CYPHER_ALLOW_FULL_SCAN=1 for whole-graph aggregate queries. Every measured query runs end-to-end through Fluree's Cypher surface (verbatim Neo4j query texts); SPARQL plays no part at query time.
fluree.durability: per-commit WAL fdatasync, durable on-disk index

load.method: native Cypher bulk importer: fluree create pokec --from pokec_<scale>_import.cypher (large: pokec_large.setup.cypher) — the same file the other engines load; bare Cypher names resolve directly, no Turtle conversion, no @vocab context
load.throughput: small 2 s; medium 24 s; large 441 s (38.8 M flakes)
load.notes: Load out of the measured path. Fresh ledger per scale.

memgraph.label: Memgraph
memgraph.config: Docker memgraph/memgraph:3.11.0, --network host, Bolt 7687. Loaded in default mode, CREATE SNAPSHOT, restarted with --data-recovery-on-startup=true --storage-wal-file-flush-every-n-tx=1 (per-commit fsync). Path queries use queries-memgraph/ overrides where the Neo4j-portable text is not accepted.

load.method: replay distribution Cypher CREATE statements through mgconsole (CREATE INDEX ON :User(id) first) -> CREATE SNAPSHOT -> restart in fsync mode
load.throughput: small 16 s; medium 252 s; large 4364 s (mgconsole replay of 30.6 M CREATE statements)
load.notes: Loaded in default mode, then restarted with per-commit WAL flushing for all published write timings. Default-mode syscall traces are retained separately.

neo4j.label: Neo4j
neo4j.config: Docker neo4j:5.26-community, --network host, Bolt 7687, heap 8G, page cache 8G, durable by default.

load.method: neo4j-admin database import full --id-type=INTEGER from CSVs generated by cypher_to_csv.py (typed header id:ID,completion_percentage:int,gender,age:int), then the User(id) index + db.awaitIndexes()
load.throughput: small 1.3 s; medium 2.4 s; large 17.5 s

falkordb.label: FalkorDB
falkordb.version: 4.20.4 (graph module ver 42004 on Redis 8.6.3; falkordb/falkordb:latest Docker image)
falkordb.config: Docker falkordb/falkordb:latest, --network host, RESP 6379. The image ships RESULTSET_SIZE 10000 and TIMEOUT 1000 (ms); both are lifted (RESULTSET_SIZE -1, TIMEOUT 0) so large expansions return full result sets — with the shipped cap, medium expansion_4 silently returned exactly 10,000 rows. Durability: Redis AOF appendfsync always, enabled after the bulk load (CONFIG SET appendonly yes / appendfsync always, verified aof_enabled:1 before measuring). Path queries use queries-falkordb/ overrides (shortestPath in WITH/RETURN; allShortestPaths in MATCH with pre-resolved endpoints, hop bound ..2).

load.method: native bulk loader falkordb-bulk-insert 1.2.0 --nodes-with-label User --relations-with-type Friend --id-type INTEGER (CSVs from cypher_to_csv.py), then explicit CREATE INDEX FOR (u:User) ON (u.id) and GRAPH.EXPLAIN verification of the index scan
load.throughput: small 0.3 s; medium 5 s; large 88 s

falkordb.memory_footprint: in-memory graph (GraphBLAS compressed-sparse); AOF/RDB is for durability and restart only, queries are never served from disk

caveats: Run 2026-09-11 on one AWS m7a.4xlarge (16c/64GB, AMD EPYC 9R14 Zen 4); single-client isolated latency; each engine on its real-world client transport, every client holding one persistent connection.
Fluree leads the read and durable-write geometric means at every scale; individual-query and category results vary. See REPORT.md section 2 for measured advantages and gaps.

Writes are apples-to-apples only because all four engines fsync per commit, verified by syscall count. Memgraph's and FalkorDB's SHIPPED defaults issue zero fsyncs over the same write pass and post sub-millisecond writes that are not comparable; they are excluded from the tables.

The July 2026 v4.1.2 report described Fluree's writes as fsync-durable; they were not. v4.1.2 file storage used tokio::fs::write with no fsync, and per-commit durability arrived in 44eb56b53 (before v4.1.6). Its ~1.3 ms small-graph write geo-mean was a page-cache number; the higher write times here are the cost of the durability every engine in this report pays; these changes prevent a direct version-to-version performance comparison.

Two reads have result-count differences. expansion_3_with_filter: small run1, Fluree/FalkorDB 3430 vs Neo4j/Memgraph 3429, with a relationship-reuse reproduction in REPORT.md. shortest_path_with_filter: small run3 FalkorDB 0 vs others 1; medium run2-run4 Memgraph 1 vs others 0. Engine-specific path queries differ. Raw TSVs record counts, not complete results. Excluding both query IDs at all scales preserves Fluree's lowest read geometric mean.

FalkorDB's official image ships RESULTSET_SIZE 10000 and TIMEOUT 1000ms; with the cap in place medium expansion_4 silently returns exactly 10000 rows. Both were lifted before measuring. Its User(id) index also builds asynchronously over minutes on the 1.6M-node graph and must be confirmed in the query plan before timing.
All graphs fit in 64 GB RAM. This single-client run does not measure concurrent throughput or performance beyond RAM capacity.
NOT comparable to Memgraph's published multi-worker throughput numbers (different mode, different hardware).
Not directly comparable to July 2026 v4.1.2 results: different hardware (r8a.4xlarge), Fluree connection handling, and write durability.

Fluree optimization targets still open: shallow-expansion batching, pattern_long, and the write path's two consistent losses: unwind_range batch writes and create__edge (match two nodes, create the edge), plus create__pattern at large; see FLUREE-GAPS.md.
